title: Smashed Cucumber & Silken Tofu Salad
style: Chinese-style cold plate — cool silken tofu under bashed cucumbers, black vinegar, chilli oil, and toasted peanuts. No cooking at all
description: A 15-minute no-cook cold plate: silken tofu spooned onto a platter, topped with salted smashed cucumbers and a black vinegar chilli-oil dressing. About 20 g protein per serving.

steps: Smash the cucumbers: Lay them on a board and hit them firmly with the flat of a wide knife or a rolling pin until they split. Tear into rough bite-size chunks — the ragged edges hold dressing far better than clean slices.
Toss the cucumber with the salt in a colander and leave 10 minutes over the sink. Discard the liquid that collects and pat dry.

Dressing — bloom the aromatics: Put the chopped garlic, gochugaru, ground Sichuan pepper, and sesame seeds in a small heatproof bowl. Heat the neutral oil in a pan until it is genuinely smoking, then pour it straight over — it should hiss and foam. This takes 20 seconds and is the difference between a sharp dressing and a deeply fragrant one.
Once the sizzling stops, stir in the soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil. Let it sit while the cucumbers drain.
Plate the tofu: Tip the chilled silken tofu onto a wide shallow plate — either as one block or spooned into big soft curds. Don't cube it neatly; broken is better here.
Pile the drained cucumbers over and around the tofu, then spoon the dressing over everything so it pools at the bottom of the plate.
Finish with peanuts, spring onions, coriander, and sesame seeds. Eat cold, right away, scooping tofu and cucumber together.
tips: Making it dinner — as written this serves 2 as a side — cucumber and silken tofu are both mostly water, so it won't hold you for long. For a proper meal either eat the whole plate yourself (~590 kcal, 40 g protein), or toss it through 150 g cold rice noodles or soba and keep it at 2 servings.

The dressing keeps in a jar in the fridge for a week and is excellent on noodles, greens, or plain rice — worth making a double batch while the oil is already hot. Skip the sizzle and use shop-bought chilli oil if you're in a hurry, but it won't be as fragrant.
Salting and draining the cucumbers is the step people skip, and it's why their salad turns into a puddle 10 minutes later.
Silken tofu straight from the fridge is essential — this dish is about temperature contrast against the hot chilli oil.
Tip the tofu out by inverting the tub onto the plate rather than lifting it; it breaks less.
Dress it at the table, not in advance. Assembled, it holds maybe 15 minutes before going watery.
Chinkiang black vinegar often contains wheat — use rice vinegar instead if you need this gluten-free, along with tamari.
